memory_verse: "He sealed us and gave us the Spirit in our hearts as a pledge." —2 Corinthians 1:22, NASB
sermon_title: JESUS: The One Greater Than Jonah

days.message_recap: Jesus transformed a blind beggar into a seeing disciple and worshiper in a single day, proving His power to completely alter any life today. While 120,000 Ninevites repented at Jonah's reluctant eight-word warning of doom, Jesus stands among us as One far greater than Jonah, drawing hearts through divine kindness and truth.
days.message_quote: The kindness of God leads us to repentance. Jonah did not come with a message of kindness. He came with a message of judgment, but yet they repented.
days.verse_reflection: If God has truly sealed you and placed His Holy Spirit in your heart as a down payment of eternal life, are you allowing that Spirit to lead your moment-by-moment attitudes, or are you still living like an orphan who reacts in self-defense, anger, and the pride of the flesh?
days.daily_prayer: Lord, thank You for sealing me with Your Holy Spirit and calling me to belong entirely to You. Search my heart today and expose every area where I still resist Your gentle leading or excuse my flesh. Grant me immediate, tender repentance whenever Your Spirit convicts me, so that Christ's life may be clearly seen in my conduct.

days.focus: Awakening from Lukewarmness and Broken Rebellion
days.message_recap: People who sat comfortably under synagogue teaching for years were suddenly shaken by deep conviction when John the Baptist preached, leaving their homes to publicly confess their hidden sins in the wilderness. Even King Manasseh, despite plunging into extreme wickedness and demonic practices, was brought by God into severe distress and captivity so that his stubborn rebellion would finally be broken.
days.message_quote: God knew what it would take to bring this man to a place of distress, a place of need, a place where this man, despite the depths of depravity or wickedness or evil, he would come to such a point where he would not fight against God anymore.
days.verse_reflection: Since the Holy Spirit in your heart is the guarantee that you belong to God and are no longer a debtor to the flesh, are you actively depending on His supernatural power to put to death the secret lusts and irritations of the body, or are you kicking against God's convictions and tolerating hidden compromise?
days.daily_prayer: Father, forgive me for the times I have sat comfortably under Your Word without allowing it to break my self-will. Break every trace of stubborn rebellion in me before I bring spiritual ruin upon myself and others. By the power of the indwelling Spirit, I choose to mortify the deeds of the flesh and walk in Your holy fear.

days.focus: True Brokenness and the Urgency of Today
days.message_recap: God heard Manasseh when he pleaded and humbled himself greatly in his affliction, proving there is hope for even the worst offender, while an upright man like Job repented in dust and ashes the moment he truly saw God. We must never delay repentance like Governor Felix did, because God exposes the secrets of our hearts so that we respond today while His voice is speaking.
days.message_quote: Today is the day of salvation. Today is the day, if you hear his voice, do not harden your hearts.
days.verse_reflection: When Job saw God, his self-righteous defense evaporated instantly into repentance in dust and ashes; does the presence of the Holy Spirit in your heart produce that same deep, daily humility that hates subtle self-justification, or do you still argue your own blamelessness whenever you are questioned or corrected?
days.daily_prayer: Lord God, deliver me from the deception of measuring myself by external uprightness while my heart remains proud and blind. Give me eyes to see You in Your holiness so that all self-righteousness is crushed to dust. Help me never to postpone obedience or harden my heart when Your Spirit speaks to me today.

days.focus: Embracing Painful Truth and Fulfilling God's Purpose
days.message_recap: Just as a trapped person might get scratched when rescued from a collapsing building or a patient must endure a surgeon's blade to be cured, God's Word often cuts us because it aims at our true spiritual salvation. The Pharisees rejected God's purpose for their lives by refusing John's baptism of repentance and constantly making excuses, finding fault with both John's fasting and Jesus' eating.
days.message_quote: How do I reject God's purpose for my life? When God speaks to me and says, 'Ajay, I want you to repent of this thing. I need you to go and set that matter right. I need you to go and apologize. I need you to forgive. I need you to go and ask for forgiveness.' And I say, 'I'm not going to do it.' What am I doing? I reject God's purpose for me.
days.verse_reflection: Knowing that God has sealed you with His Spirit as a pledge that sin shall no longer have dominion over you, are you presenting your members as instruments of righteousness, or do you reject God's purpose by clinging to stubborn grudges, refusing to apologize, and excusing your un-Christlike reactions?
days.daily_prayer: Lord Jesus, I do not want to frustrate Your gracious purpose for my life through excuses, wounded pride, or resentment. When Your truth cuts deep into my conscience, give me the grace to yield immediately and make matters right. Thank You that through Your Spirit, sin has no right to rule over my mortal body.

days.focus: Hearing God's Word and Welcoming Truth-Tellers
days.message_recap: Abraham told the rich man in torment that those who refuse to hear the written Word of God will not repent even if someone returns from the dead, exposing the folly of waiting for sensational signs or a flattering preacher. King Ahab hated Micaiah because the prophet spoke painful truth rather than pleasing lies, leaving the king without excuse when judgment fell.
days.message_quote: If they do not listen to Moses and the prophets, if they can't hear to the ordinary words of God spoken when they read God's word or when it's preached to them, if they don't repent at that, even if we have a person here raised from the dead this morning, they will not repent.
days.verse_reflection: The Spirit of God dwelling within us is given to testify to Christ by producing obedience to His commandments; are you genuinely submitted to His voice through the Scriptures and through godly believers who correct you, or do you resent those who tell you the plain truth about your spiritual condition?
days.daily_prayer: Heavenly Father, keep me from the spiritual blindness of Ahab, who surrounded himself with flatterers and despised the voice of truth. Teach me to tremble at Your written Word and to welcome with deep gratitude anyone who loves my soul enough to point out my blind spots. Let Your Spirit keep my conscience tender and thoroughly obedient.

days.focus: The True Blessing: Turning from Wicked Ways
days.message_recap: While Ahab shut his ears to Micaiah and perished, Peter humbly received sharp public correction from Paul because his heart had an open door toward God and toward those watching over his soul. The true scriptural blessing of God is revealed in Acts 3:26 as Jesus being sent to turn each person away from their wicked ways, granting the life-giving repentance that makes room for the Holy Spirit.
days.message_quote: God raised his servant Jesus and sent him to bless you by turning every one of you from your wicked ways.
days.verse_reflection: If the Holy Spirit whom God placed within you yearns jealously over your heart, are you drawing near to God in humble brokenness so that He can lift you up, or are you settling for a superficial religious blessing while stubbornly holding onto the double-minded ways of the world?
days.daily_prayer: Lord Jesus, I ask for the true blessing of God: that You would completely turn my heart away from every subtle wickedness and selfish motive. Grant me a teachable spirit like Peter, ready to receive correction and eager to walk in practical purity. Cleanse my hands, purify my heart, and fill me afresh with Your Holy Spirit to live entirely for Your glory.
